sentences.text: 3. Prosecution story, in brief is that at the time of incident, prosecutrix was aged about more than 16 years.
On 03.03.2020, when the prosecutrix returning home from grocery store, in the way, the applicant forcibly took the prosecutrix by motorcycle and took her in a room for around a year.
Meanwhile, he committed rape upon her repeatedly.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant/accused submits that the applicant has not committed the offence and he has falsely been implicated in the case.
It is submitted that earlier parents of the prosecutrix had lodged two FIRs relating to rape against the applicant, wherein the applicant has been acquitted by the Competent Authority.
Thereafter, this third FIR was also falsely lodged against the applicant stating different place, but likewise same offence.
5. It is further submitted that after dismissal of his first bail application, prosecutrix (PW-1) and her father (PW-2) have been examined before the Trial Court.
Though the prosecutrix supported the prosecution case in her examination-in-chief, but she has denied prosecution story in her cross- examination.
In re-examination-in-chief, she has also admitted that he had given false evidence in her examination-in-chief.
Therefore, involvement of the applicant in the crime is doubtful.
6. It is submitted that applicant is in custody since 12.12.2022.
Trial will take considerable long time for its disposal, therefore, it is prayed that the applicant be released on bail.
7. On the other hand, learned counsel for the non-applicant/State has opposed the prayer and prayed for its rejection.
8. Learned counsel for the objector has pleaded that he has no objection if the applicant is granted bail.

9. Having considered the rival submissions and after perusal of the case diary so also considering the facts and circumstances of the case, without commenting on the merits of the case, this Court is of the view that applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail hence, the application is allowed.

10. It is directed that the applicant - Ajay shall be released on bail upon his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned Trial Court for his appearance before the Trial Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this behalf by the Trial Court during pendency of the trial.
It is further directed that applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.
11. This order shall be effective till the end of trial but in case of bail jump, it shall become ineffective.
12. With the aforesaid, this application is allowed and stands disposed of.
